title: cubic blog: What Code Review Tools Learn from a Senior Engineer's Past Pull Request Comments and Apply That Context Automatically to Future Reviews?
summary: What AI code review is, how it works on a pull request, what it catches and misses, and how to tell a useful AI code reviewer from a noisy one.
body_markdown:
## The best AI code review tools in 2026


On Martian’s board the top five sit within about three F1 points, so choose on fit: which Git hosts a tool supports, how it bills, and where it runs. Prices are as of October 2026, from each vendor’s pricing page.


-


### cubic


#1 on Martian


Our product. Reads each pull request with context from your repository, docs and tickets, learns from your senior reviewers’ past comments, and, on Pro and Max, fixes issues when you ask. GitHub only. Free for public repositories; paid plans from $30 per developer a month billed yearly.


[Pricing](https://www.cubic.dev/pricing-plans)


-


### Kody AI


#2 on Martian


Kodus’s open-source (AGPL) reviewer, listed as Kody AI on Martian’s board, for GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Gitea and Forgejo. Self-host it for free, or use the hosted Teams plan at $8 per developer a month billed yearly, plus your own model tokens.


[Pricing](https://kodus.io/pricing)


-


### Greptile


#3 on Martian


Builds a graph of your repository and reviews each pull request against it. Runs on GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket in its cloud, with self-hosting on Enterprise. $30 per seat a month includes 50 credits; a Base review costs one credit, a Plus or Apex review three or ten, and each extra credit costs $1.


[Pricing](https://www.greptile.com/pricing)[CodeRabbit vs Greptile](https://www.cubic.dev/blog/coderabbit-vs-greptile)


-


### CodeRabbit


#4 on Martian


Runs dozens of linters and security scanners alongside its AI review, on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps. From $24 per developer a month billed yearly, and free for public repositories.


[Our CodeRabbit review](https://www.cubic.dev/blog/coderabbit-review)[cubic vs CodeRabbit](https://www.cubic.dev/vs/coderabbit)


-


### Claude


#5 on Martian


Anthropic’s GitHub reviewer. Its managed Code Review, a research preview on Team and Enterprise plans, averages[$15-25 per review](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review#pricing) , billed as usage. For most teams that isn’t worth paying for; run Claude Code’s local` /code-review` before you push instead.


[Our Claude Code review](https://www.cubic.dev/blog/claude-code-review)


cubic reviews GitHub only. On GitLab or Bitbucket, start with Kodus, Greptile or CodeRabbit; on Azure DevOps, Kodus or CodeRabbit. Our[full ranked list](https://www.cubic.dev/best-ai-code-review-tools) covers more tools, and our head-to-head pages compare[cubic with CodeRabbit, GitHub Copilot, Cursor Bugbot, Qodo, Codacy and Sourcery](https://www.cubic.dev/vs) .
